name: Auto Union Type C
description:
Auto Union Type C

Grand Prix 750 kg
Design: Ferdinand Porsche
Engine: V16 45°, 75 x 85 mm = 6006 cc, Roots supercharger, 520 bhp @ 5000 rpm
Transmission: 5 speed
Suspension: front: trailing links with torsion bars, rear: swing axles with transverse leaf spring
Dimensions: wheelbase 2909 mm, track 1397 mm, 315 km/h
Years: 1936-1937

The last and largest of Porsche's mid-engined V16s, the bore taken out to 75 mm for 6006 cc - the biggest engine anyone ran under the 750 kg formula. The fuel sat between the driver and the engine, so the balance shifted as the tank emptied, which is a large part of why these cars were so feared. In 1936 it hardly mattered: Auto Union won six of the twelve major races and Bernd Rosemeyer, who took five of them, was crowned European Champion. It was still winning in 1937 - the Eifelrennen, Coppa Acerbo, Donington and the Vanderbilt Cup - but by then the Mercedes W125 had moved the standard out of reach.
author: Gary Paterson
